src/duration.js:170: * A Duration object represents a period of time, like "2 months" or "1 day, 1 hour". Conceptually, it's just a map of units to their quantities, accompanied by some additional configuration and methods for creating, parsing, interrogating, transforming, and formatting them. They can be used on their own or in conjunction with other Luxon types; for example, you can use {@link DateTime#plus} to add a Duration object to a DateTime, producing another DateTime.

src/duration.js:174: * * **Creation** To create a Duration, use {@link Duration.fromMillis}, {@link Duration.fromObject}, or {@link Duration.fromISO}.

src/duration.js:176: * * **Configuration** See  {@link Duration#locale} and {@link Duration#numberingSystem} accessors.

docs/math.md:136:## Duration math
docs/math.md:140:`Durations` are quantities of time, like "3 days and 6 hours". Luxon has no idea *which* 3 days and 6 hours they represent; it's just how Luxon represents those quantities in abstract, unmoored from the timeline. This is both tremendously useful and occasionally confusing. I'm not going to give a detailed tour of their capabilities here (see the API docs for that), but I do want to clear up some of those confusions.
docs/math.md:145:var dur = Duration.fromObject({ days: 3, hours: 6})
docs/math.md:162:You can subtract one time from another to find out how much time there is between them. Luxon's `DateTime.diff` method does this and it returns a Duration. For example:
docs/math.md:189:Durations represent bundles of time with specific units, but Luxon allows you to convert between them:
docs/math.md:191: * `shiftTo` returns a new Duration denominated in the specified units.
docs/math.md:195:var dur = Duration.fromObject({ months: 4, weeks: 2, days: 6 })
docs/math.md:221:Duration.fromObject({ years:1 }).shiftTo('months').shiftTo('days').as('years') //=> 0.9863013698630136
docs/math.md:227:var dur = Duration.fromObject({ years: 50000 });
docs/math.md:242:Luxon methods that create Durations de novo accept an option called `conversionAccuracy`. You can set it to "casual" or "longterm". It's a property of the Duration itself, so any conversions you do use the rule you've picked, and any new Durations you derive from it will retain that property.
docs/math.md:245:Duration.fromObject({ years: 23 }, { conversionAccuracy: 'longterm' });
docs/math.md:246:Duration.fromISO('PY23', { conversionAccuracy: 'longterm' });
docs/math.md:251:You can also create an accurate Duration out of an existing one:
docs/math.md:254:var pedanticDuration = casualDuration.reconfigure({ conversionAccuracy: 'longterm' });
docs/math.md:257:These Durations will do their conversions differently.
docs/math.md:280:It's important to remember that diffs are Duration objects, and a Duration is just a dumb pile of time units our computation spat out. Unlike an Interval, a Duration doesn't "remember" what the inputs to the diff were. So we lost some information converting between units. This mistake is really common when rolling up:
docs/math.md:311:Because the Interval stores its endpoints and computes `length` on the fly, it retakes the diff each time you query it. Of course, precisely because an Interval *isn't* an abstract bundle of time, it can't be used in places where Durations can. For example, you can't add them to DateTime via `plus()` because Luxon wouldn't know what units to do the math in (see "Calendar vs time math" above). But you can convert the interval into a Duration by picking the units:
docs/math.md:314:i.toDuration('months').toObject(); //=> { months: 1 }
docs/math.md:315:i.toDuration('days').toObject(); //=> { days: 28 }
docs/math.md:323:i.toDuration(['years', 'months', 'days']).toObject(); //=> { years: 1, months: 3, days: 12 }
docs/math.md:326:Of course, once you've converted to a Duration, you're back in the same spot you were with the diff case; *further* conversions will be lossy. So the point is to think carefully about what information you have when.
docs/tour.md:170:## Durations
docs/tour.md:172:The Duration class represents a quantity of time such as "2 hours and 7 minutes". You create them like this:
docs/tour.md:175:var dur = Duration.fromObject({ hours: 2, minutes: 7 });
docs/tour.md:200:You can also format, negate, and normalize them. See it all in the `Duration` API docs.
docs/home.md:13: * Duration support (14 days, 5 minutes, 33 seconds)
docs/intl.md:50:By default, the `locale` property of a new DateTime or Duration is the system locale. On a browser, that means whatever the user has their browser or OS language set to. On Node, that usually means en-US.
docs/validity.md:78:## Invalid Durations
docs/validity.md:80:Durations can be invalid too. The easiest way to get one is to diff an invalid DateTime.
docs/validity.md:91:- It was created from invalid DateTime or Duration
docs/upgrading.md:33:`DateTime.fromObject()` and `Duration.fromObject()` now accept two parameters: one for the object and one for the options.
docs/upgrading.md:40:Duration.fromObject({ hours: 3, minutes: 2, conversionAccuracy: "casual", locale: "ru" });
docs/upgrading.md:44:Duration.fromObject({ hours: 3, minutes: 2 }, { conversionAccuracy: "casual", locale: "ru" });
docs/moment.md:29:1. Luxon has both a Duration type and an Interval type. The Interval type is like Twix.
docs/moment.md:38:1. Luxon's Durations are a separate top-level class.
docs/moment.md:147:| Duration         | `diff(Moment)` | `diff(DateTime)`            | Moment's diff returns a count of milliseconds, but Luxon's returns a Duration. To replicate the Moment behavior, use `dt1.diff(d2).milliseconds`. |
docs/moment.md:161:## Durations
docs/moment.md:163:Moment Durations and Luxon Durations are broadly similar in purpose and capabilities. The main differences are:
docs/moment.md:165:1.  Luxon durations have more sophisticated conversion capabilities. They can convert from one set of units to another using `shiftTo`. They can also be configured to use different unit conversions. See [Duration Math](math.md?id=duration-math) for more.
docs/moment.md:166:1.  Luxon does not (yet) have an equivalent of Moment's Duration `humanize` method. Luxon will add that when [Intl.UnitFormat](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-intl-unit-format) is supported by browsers.
docs/moment.md:167:1.  Like DateTimes, Luxon Durations have separate methods for creating objects from different sources.
docs/moment.md:169:See the `Duration` API docs for more.
